title: Harbor and Bakery
premise: Vesper Lockridge has spent fifteen years building Salt & Ember, a tiny harbor-town bakery, after a public humiliation in her famous culinary family taught her to keep her head down. When her mother demands she bring a date to the Lockridge vineyard's reunion, she hires Callum Reyes—a charming, quietly adrift sommelier who once left a scathing review of her pastries—posing as her boyfriend. What begins as a transaction deepens into real intimacy, but Callum's secret connection to the investor deciding her bakery's fate threatens everything she's built. At the vineyard's first harvest festival, Vesper must choose between protecting her safe, invisible life and risking her heart and reputation on the truth.
about_author: J. M. Sandoval is a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, vineyards, and coastal towns where everyone knows your order. She lives near the water with her partner, two opinionated cats, and a sourdough starter older than her career.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Opening on a pre-dawn bake, we learn Salt & Ember is three missed payments from closure and the bank wants answers by month's end. Vesper's careful, controlled life is established in sensory detail. Emotional beat: quiet dread masked by routine competence.

chapters.title: The Letter with the Wax Seal
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. An invitation to the Lockridge family reunion arrives—her mother's handwriting, a plus-one required, a reminder that her sister's engagement will be the centerpiece. Vesper's hands shake kneading dough. Emotional beat: old shame resurfacing, the cost of fifteen years of invisibility.

chapters.title: One Star, Extra Salt
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum Reyes, newly arrived in Harbor's End and between careers, recognizes the bakery from a review he wrote years ago—one star, cruelly worded, written in a bitter season he regrets. He orders a croissant to apologize to no one in particular. Emotional beat: guilt and restless drift.

chapters.title: A Transaction, Not a Romance
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper overhears Callum confess his review to her counter girl and, impulsively, offers him a deal: be her fake date to the reunion, and she'll pay him from her dwindling funds. He agrees, amused. Emotional beat: desperation dressed up as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Over stolen evenings in the closed bakery, they build their fake history—how they met, first date, inside jokes. The rehearsal feels dangerously like real courtship. Emotional beat: reluctant delight, the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: The Drive to Lockridge Hill
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The drive to the vineyard, Callum's hand steady on hers, the family estate rising out of the fog. Vesper coaches him through the gauntlet of aunts and cousins. Emotional beat: armor going on, and Callum seeing straight through it.

chapters.title: The Engagement Toast
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Dinner under the vines: her sister Margot announces her engagement, her mother delivers a backhanded compliment about Vesper's 'little shop,' and Callum defends her baking with unexpected passion. Emotional beat: fury, then the shock of being publicly championed.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Dual POV. After dinner, they escape to the cellar and share a stolen bottle. The fake-date script dissolves; a near-kiss is interrupted by Margot. Emotional beat: the lie curdling into longing neither will name.

chapters.title: What Callum Knows
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum recognizes the reunion's guest of honor—Alder Financial's Marcus Webb, the investor deciding Salt & Ember's loan fate—and realizes Vesper's bakery hangs on a man who knows his old review. He says nothing. Emotional beat: the secret taking root.

chapters.title: Sunday Croissants
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Back home, Callum becomes a fixture at the bakery—fixing the awning, tasting test batches, learning her rhythms. The town begins assuming they're together. Emotional beat: domestic warmth she never planned for, and won't examine.

chapters.title: The Investor's Card
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Marcus Webb contacts Callum, offering a sommelier position in the city—and casually asking about the Lockridge daughter's business prospects. Callum realizes his silence could save or sink her. Emotional beat: loyalty and self-interest at war.

chapters.title: Margot's Warning
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Margot visits the bakery, ostensibly to reconcile, and needles Vesper about the 'sudden' boyfriend. The sisters' old wound—Margot's rise built on Vesper's fall—opens. Emotional beat: grief for the sisterhood they lost, suspicion she can't voice.

chapters.title: First Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The vineyard's first harvest approaches and the family gathers early. Callum, now genuinely in love, plans to confess his review and his Webb connection. Vesper, sensing distance, braces for abandonment. Emotional beat: two people orbiting the same truth, missing each other.

chapters.title: The Review Resurfaces
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Margot, digging for leverage, finds Callum's old review and shows Vesper: the man beside her once tried to destroy her. Vesper confronts him in the vineyard rows. Emotional beat: betrayal, the old story rewriting itself—everyone leaves, everyone lies.

chapters.title: What I Was Then
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum tells the full truth: the review, the year of grief behind it, and the Webb connection he hid to protect her. He offers to walk away. Vesper, unable to hear him over her own fear, lets him. Emotional beat: heartbreak that feels like self-protection.

chapters.title: The Bakery Goes Dark
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Without Callum, and with the bank's deadline arriving, Vesper closes the bakery for a day and faces the ledger—and herself. She realizes she's been choosing smallness since she was twenty-five. Emotional beat: the turning inward before the turn outward.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper confronts her mother about the humiliation that exiled her fifteen years ago—and learns it was Margot's sabotage her mother covered up. The family mythology cracks. Emotional beat: rage, then a hard-won release from the old verdict on her name.

chapters.title: Harvest Day
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The first harvest festival: Webb tours the vineyard, Margot's engagement party doubles as a business showcase, and Callum arrives uninvited to tell Vesper one more truth—Webb's offer to him was contingent on her bakery failing. Emotional beat: the climax's fuse lit in public.

chapters.title: The Truth, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Before the assembled family and investors, Vesper exposes Webb's scheme and Margot's old sabotage, then—terrified—declares what Salt & Ember is worth, and what Callum is to her. Emotional beat: the invisible woman made visible, stakes fully risked.

chapters.title: After the Shouting
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Fallout: Webb withdraws, Margot's engagement wobbles, and Callum, believing his presence cost Vesper everything, prepares to leave Harbor's End. Vesper finds him at the ferry dock. Emotional beat: love choosing itself over safety, at last.

chapters.title: Salt & Ember, Reopened
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The bank, moved by the festival's publicity and a community micro-loan Vesper finally allows herself to accept, restructures the debt. The bakery reopens with a new sign, a new partner in the kitchen, and Callum's old review framed—crossed out to five stars. Emotional beat: belonging, earned.

chapters.title: First Loaf of the Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Weeks later, dawn at the vineyard: the harvest is in, the family is tentatively mending, and Vesper and Callum bake bread in the estate kitchen for the workers. She proposes nothing and everything at once; he says yes to staying. Emotional beat: quiet joy, the safe step finally taken together.
